expectations.text: Business logic is separated from HTTP concerns — there is at least a distinct service/handler layer separate from the route
expectations.evidence: All logic (validation + db call) is inline in the route handler. db.js is a data layer but there is no service layer separating business logic from HTTP.

expectations.text: Request body is validated before reaching any business logic, using a schema or explicit checks
expectations.evidence: Explicit validation checks for customerId, items array, and each item's productId and quantity before calling db.orders.create

expectations.text: Errors are explicitly caught and handled — no unhandled promise rejections or try/catch-less async
expectations.evidence: Entire handler wrapped in try/catch with explicit 500 response

expectations.text: Internal error details (stack traces, DB errors) are not exposed in the HTTP response
expectations.evidence: catch block only logs err and returns a generic 'An unexpected error occurred' message

expectations.text: Returns 201 on success and 400 on validation failure (not just 200 for everything)
expectations.evidence: res.status(201).json(order) on success; res.status(400).json({ error: ... }) on validation failure
